lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.29 - A Match and write

details: Match and write develops writing accuracy by helping students complete key vocabulary about family members using visual prompts and word gaps.
Look for correct answers based on the images shown, and neat handwriting.
“I need you to be undercover detectives today, class. There’s a new family in town! Can you figure out who they are and what they’re doing, without them seeing you?”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.29 - B. Listen and choose

details: Listen and choose develops students’ ability to connect vocabulary with visual clues, using audio support to help build word recognition.
Look for careful listening, accurate recognition of key vocabulary and correct picture choices.
“Great work. Your next job, detectives, is to listen for clues, We need to know which of these pictures is right.”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.83 - A Find and circle

details: Find and circle develops students’ ability to recognise and locate key vocabulary about family members and activities in a wordsearch. The activity reinforces spelling and reading skills.
Look for students carefully scanning the wordsearch, correctly circling target words and staying engaged with the task.
“Time to use your brains, detectives. These words have all hidden in the wordsearch. Can you find them?” .

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.83 - B Look and tick

details: Look and tick develops writing accuracy and comprehension by helping students match pictures of fruit and vegetables to the correct singular or plural response to a question. The activity reinforces vocabulary and basic grammar.
Look for correct matching of questions and answers, students recognising the difference between one and more than one item. and neat bookwork.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.30 - Speaking My Family Tree

details: My Family Tree develops listening and questioning skills as students play the game and describe a family member. Students use key vocabulary in question and answer form and practise speaking skills in a playful context.
Look for strong teamwork, students asking and answering questions using correct vocabulary, careful listening and showing engagement and confidence in guessing the cards.
“Brilliant job, everyone. Your last detective task is to find out who all these people are. Can you ask and answer questions?”
